item.title: Researchers escape OpenAI Codex sandbox to run commands on host
item.description: Problem: OpenAI's Codex coding agent sandboxes untrusted code, but researchers found two ways out. Approach: "Heapjack" abused node_repl, which runs trusted and untrusted JS in one process sharing one memory heap — attackers used V8's getHeapSnapshot() to read a validation token out of memory and reuse it to message the unsandboxed parent. "Overpatch" abused the CLI's apply_patch tool: naming /tmp in a patch widened write permissions via symlinks. Result: Both worked even in Codex's most restrictive modes, achieving host code execution. OpenAI patched both within 8 days. Why it matters: The enforcement logic lived inside the thing it was supposed to police — the same pattern turned up in Cursor and Gemini CLI. Glossary: Sandbox - a restricted execution environment for untrusted code. Heap - a program's shared pool of dynamic memory. Symlink - a file that points to another path. Validation token - a secret string proving a request is authorized.

item.title: SolarWinds Patches ARM Hard-Coded Key Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
item.description: A hard-coded cryptographic key in SolarWinds ARM let anyone forge requests for unauthenticated remote code execution; patch now, unpatched instances are trivially exploitable.

item.title: Malicious npm packages evade install-script defenses at runtime
item.description: Packages now trigger their payload after install completes instead of during it, dodging scanners that only watch install-time scripts.

item.title: Elden Ring Nightreign is dead, but modders are dabbing on its corpse, with one porting an entire Dark Souls 2 DLC zone as a playable map
item.description: With official support over, modders are extending Nightreign's life by porting whole DLC content from other FromSoftware games into it.

item.title: Hideo Kojima says he was 'shocked' after Sony cut ties with Physint over a Zoom call
item.description: Kojima says Sony ended the Physint partnership abruptly over video call, the latest sign of Sony pulling back from original-IP bets.

item.title: Cooling liquids reveal self-limiting particle clusters behind glass transition
item.description: Simulations show particle clusters in supercooled liquids grow only to a self-limiting size before collapsing, helping explain why liquids resist crystallizing into glass.

item.title: T. rex teeth indicate it ran as warm as an elephant
item.description: Oxygen-isotope analysis of T. rex tooth enamel points to body temperatures and metabolic rates comparable to a modern elephant.

item.title: Resident Evil 4 (GameCube) – complete byte-identical decompilation to C/C++
item.description: A community project has finished a full, byte-identical decompilation of the GameCube original, opening the source to modding, ports, and preservation.

item.title: Reviving TEMPEST Attacks with an Injected Signal
item.description: Problem: Classic TEMPEST eavesdropping reads a device's own stray radio emissions, but modern low-power electronics barely emit any. Approach: The InjectEave technique instead transmits an RF signal tuned to a target's internal antennas; nonlinear parts inside (amplifiers, ADCs, switching MOSFETs) mix that signal with the device's internal data, radiating sidebands an attacker can demodulate with an SDR. Result: With a USRP B210 SDR and spectrum analyzer, the team recovered headphone and VoIP audio and smart-device on/off states, up to 30m through walls with a power amp — enough audio, they note, to clone a voice. Why it matters: It shows electromagnetic side-channel eavesdropping still works on "quiet" hardware, via an active attack that's harder to design against than passive TEMPEST. Glossary: TEMPEST - eavesdropping via a device's unintended electromagnetic emissions. SDR - software-defined radio. Sideband - a frequency band created when two signals mix. Nonlinear component - a circuit part whose output isn't proportional to its input.

item.title: No GPU, No Problem: Flagship LLMs on a GPU-less Teenaged Server
item.description: A hobbyist ran current flagship-scale LLMs entirely on CPU on an old rack server, documenting the RAM and throughput tradeoffs that make it viable.
